Targeting and post attachments are in place, and all three posts were approved. I'm activating the campaign and the three line items now, since you authorized the launch.
The campaign is live and all three line items are active. Next I'll let it run a few hours, then check delivery.

Early numbers are small. Over about 12 hours, the three line items have 17, 13 and 26 link clicks, with spend of about $10.51, $8.67 and $13.71. I'll hold off on changes until there's a full day of data.

The Havlumi Valentine campaign ran for the full flight, Monday Feb 8 to Sunday Feb 14, 2027 (Singapore time). It has now expired and isn't serving. X can't see installs, so the numbers below are link clicks, which are only a step toward installs. I have no install counts; those need to come from your app reporting.

**Recap (Feb 8–14, 2027 SGT, all three posts, iOS only, China excluded)**

| Post | Spend | Impressions | Link clicks | Cost per link click |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Everyday strip (2150262900128148936) | $146.77 | 426,704 | 244 | $0.60 |
| Valentine Keepsake Pack (2150444094061922123) | $146.47 | 437,194 | 226 | $0.65 |
| Save one collage (2150625287996295112) | $222.83 | 523,038 | 449 | $0.50 |
| **Total** | **$516.07** | **1,386,936** | **919** | **$0.56** |

Of the $550 budget, $33.93 went unspent.

**Observations**

- **Save one collage was the strongest.** It got the most link clicks at the lowest cost, and it stayed cheapest throughout. On Feb 10 I moved budget toward it (lifetime caps went to $230 for it and $155 each for the other two). The total still came to $540 of the $550 budget.
- **The Keepsake Pack post was the most expensive per click,** even though its message is the one with the Feb 14 deadline. Its clicks could still lead to installs, but the cost difference is small.
- **Installs are the gap.** X can't see installs, and the three posts all link to the same page, so the click numbers can't show which post drove which installs. To tell them apart, give each post its own tracked link, such as separate UTM parameters or a page variant, and compare installs against those links in your app reporting.
- **The campaign name is misleading.** It says "iPhone installs," but the objective is link clicks, since there's no app-install campaign or pixel here. I left the name as it is; tell me if you'd like it changed.
